content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Incident Response and Digital Forensics (IRDF) Technical Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Incident Response and Digital Forensics (IRDF) represents a critical framework within cybersecurity designed to detect, contain, investigate, and remediate cyber threats. This tutorial covers the foundational phases and technical practices required to perform effective forensic analysis."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 1: Preparation and Readiness"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before an incident occurs, organizations must establish an Incident Response Plan (IRP), deploy monitoring tools, and ensure forensic readiness. This includes configuring logging mechanisms and maintaining isolated golden images for system restoration."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 2: Identification and Containment"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"When suspicious activity is detected, analysts must rapidly identify the scope of the compromise. Containment strategies are then implemented to prevent lateral movement without destroying volatile evidence."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Network Isolation: Disconnect compromised hosts from the local area network while maintaining remote management capabilities if necessary."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Process Suspension: Terminate malicious processes identified through endpoint detection tools."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 3: Acquisition and Digital Forensics"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Digital forensics requires strict adherence to the chain of custody. Volatile data (RAM, active network connections) must be collected before non-volatile data (hard disk drives, solid-state drives)."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"dd if=/dev/sda of=/mnt/forensic_drive/suspect_image.raw bs=64K conv=noerror,sync"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The command above creates a bit-stream image of a storage drive while handling read errors gracefully, ensuring data integrity for subsequent analysis."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 4: Analysis and Eradication"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"During analysis, investigators parse file systems, examine registry keys, inspect log files, and analyze memory dumps for artifacts left by attackers. Once the root cause is identified, eradication steps remove malware, close vulnerabilities, and revoke compromised credentials."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"volatility -f mem_dump.raw --profile=Win10x64_19041 pslist"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Using memory forensics tools like Volatility allows analysts to list processes running at the time of memory acquisition, exposing hidden or injected processes."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 5: Recovery and Lessons Learned"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"The final phase involves restoring systems to normal operations, monitoring for reinfection, and conducting a post-incident review. The post-incident report documents timelines, indicators of compromise (IoCs), and recommendations for security posture improvement."}]
